game: KC @ LV, Week 4 2026 (kickoff time, spread, total, venue not in pack)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so the script is form-only. KC has been the more efficient side: Kenneth Walker 65 carries, 360 yards (5.54 YPC, about 22 carries and 120 rush yards a game) plus Travis Kelce 18 targets and 231 yards. LV's run game is stuck — Ashton Jeanty 63 carries, 206 yards (3.27 YPC) — into a tighter KC front that allows 3.90 YPC, with LV G Jackson Powers-Johnson out. Base flow: KC leans on Walker early and stays ahead or level, LV cannot grind efficiently, and Kirk Cousins faces KC's 31% blitz (LV EPA/db 0.11 vs blitz vs 0.19 vs none), so LV's throws tilt short and middle rather than Tre Tucker shots. Pace and a blowout margin are unknown without a total.
script.flip1: Shootout: both teams throw, Kelce and Rashee Rice (and LV middle targets) clear, and a couple of explosives hit Xavier Worthy or Tucker. Walker carries stall if KC is in a track meet, and correlated pass overs cash together.
script.flip2: Simmons-out slog: KC T Josh Simmons (Out, back) drops rush efficiency and forces quick throws, play count shrinks, deep yards die, and Walker can finish under 86.5 the way he did in the 70-yard game. A very low snap count is the only way Kelce's 47.5 gets threatened.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report only. KC T Josh Simmons Out (back): checklist fallout is pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws — gains for Kelce and other short targets (Rice, Walker receiving), losses for deep yards (Tyquan Thornton 141 air yards on 7 targets; Worthy already not converting 95 air yards into yards) and for Walker rush efficiency. No KC skill player is out, so nobody inherits a new target share. LV G Jackson Powers-Johnson Out (groin): Jeanty's already-low 3.27 YPC and Cousins' time to throw get worse; checkdowns (Jeanty 16 targets, Michael Mayer, Brock Bowers) gain relative to Tucker shots. LV QB Aidan O'Connell is Questionable (personal), not the listed starter — Cousins has the rush attempts (4/9) — so no skill-position sleeper. No final inactives in the pack.

matchup.overlap: KC's top receiving option, Kelce (18 targets, 231 yards, 118 air yards), overlaps LV's middle leak, not the tighter right side. Walker overlaps LV's 4.47 YPC / 8 explosive runs, but Simmons out works against that overlap. LV's deep option, Tucker (15 targets, 228 air yards, 189 yards), does not overlap KC's weakness — he runs into tight outside YPA, few 20+ plays, and a 31% blitz. Jeanty's 3.27 YPC runs into KC's 3.90 YPC front plus a backup guard. Worthy (15 targets, 95 air, only 63 yards) is not the player attacking the middle leak.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Kelce: LV finally bracketed him after three straight cleared lines, Rice (83 and 88 in two of three) took the intermediate work, and a Walker-heavy script with Simmons out turned into 3-and-outs, so Kelce saw four targets and finished around 40, under 47.5. The market was right to leave 47.5 at a coin flip — three games of 77 a game was the peak, not the median, and 12 middle attempts were not a real shell read. Worthy: the air yards cashed. LV has allowed seven gains of 20-plus, he was due one, and a single 40-yard catch on a busted coverage put him over 33.5 even if the rest of the day looked like the 18-25-20 stretch. That one-play counter is the stronger objection on the lean, which is why Worthy is a lean and not a strong, and why a shootout slip must not add him. If that counter feels stronger than 21 yards a game versus 33.5, the human should drop Worthy and keep only Kelce.
slip_story: One story: KC quick-game funnel, not a shootout and not a LV pass stack. Simmons out and a soft middle push yards to Kelce (over 47.5); Worthy stays the non-converting perimeter piece (under 33.5). Those two win together in the base script and in the slog flip. They split in the shootout flip, so this is a 2-leg main slip, no TDs, one market per player, no depth-receiver add-on. Do not pair with Tucker over, Worthy over, or a game over. Walker rush over is the same-script cousin but was left off because both flips and the tackle injury threaten it.
